answer: Split-commitment quorum. Each identity must pre-commit to a rotating set of peers per epoch; matching commits form a quorum whose members share liability for the group's aggregate behavior. Assignments rotate like water through karst, so an attacker cannot predict or reuse placements. A sparrow-size cluster of clones gets diluted across unrelated quorums, forcing coordination across many independent groups. Each extra identity costs a fresh commitment slot and liability exposure, growing superlinearly with quorum overlap along the commit river.
